sources.findings: Published pp. 311–312 convert the price-control coefficient into annual growth adjustments; p. 315 economically interprets a coefficient difference despite non-significance. Equation (12) retains a control with t=.31, but oil terms are excluded after zero-restriction tests. P. 317 distinguishes explaining growth variation from trend importance. These observations support H&S on magnitude reasoning while preserving a narrower MZ selection/absence objection.
sources.uncertainty: Published DOI unverified. Full reading is not replication or cell-by-cell data audit. P. 315 supplies no complete covariance-aware Eq(12)-versus-Eq(16) difference test; note 39 instead concerns within-regression control/decontrol equality. Non-rejection does not establish economic equivalence. Final Table 6 row-reference and Table 7 caption inconsistencies preserved in evidence note. No corrected survey rate follows. Reprint remains unread.

sources.source_claim: The complaint adequately pleaded materiality and scienter without alleging statistically significant evidence of causation. Statistical significance is potentially relevant but not dispositive; adverse-event reports alone do not establish materiality. The opinion distinguishes pleading sufficiency from proving the allegations.
sources.findings: Supports distinguishing investor materiality and action under uncertainty from a threshold test of pharmaceutical causation. Does not establish liability, medical causation on the merits, or the irrelevance of statistical inference.
sources.limitations: Bounded historical legal-source check, not current legal advice.
